customManagers.description: The supervisor ref the validate:apps task fetches schemas from (mise.toml [vars].supervisor_ref; see .mise/tasks/validate/apps.py). Tracks home-assistant/supervisor GitHub releases: validating against the newest release keeps the app configs ahead of the installed fleet (stable-channel rollout lags releases). PRs automerge once the CI check job is green – green means the new schemas validate our app configs.

The hk@X.Y.Z pkl package that hk.pkl imports (amends + Builtins lines) must move together with the hk pin in mise.toml [tools] and mise.lock – the package provides the builtin step definitions the binary executes. The mise manager owns mise.toml + mise.lock; this manager keeps hk.pkl in the SAME update: same depName, datasource and currentValue as the mise manager's hk dep, so Renovate folds both into one branch and one PR bumps all three files. Two matchStrings because each import line carries the version twice (path segment and hk@X# marker) and both occurrences must be rewritten – the same invariant bump-hk.sh enforces for manual bumps. The CI check catches partial desyncs regardless: mise install --locked errors when mise.toml and mise.lock disagree.

packageRules.description: Alpine apk pins in app Dockerfiles (e.g. hd-idle=1.22-r8): read the apk datasource's versions from the Alpine binary repositories and bump the app's config.yaml version in the same PR (experimental bumpVersions feature; generic for all apps). Renovate cannot infer the branch from the base-image ARG default – without registryUrls it silently skips these pins (skipReason unknown-registry) – so the branch is pinned here; update it together with the Dockerfile BUILD_FROM default on a base-image bump (the validate:apk-pins drift check derives the branch dynamically and cross-checks the pins either way). The changelog entry for the bumped version is filled post-merge by the apk-bump workflow (CI; the hosted Renovate app cannot run post-upgrade tasks). Merge behavior and grouping are decided per update type by the chained apk rules below – see the repository-root KNOWLEDGE.md apk package version policy.

bumpVersions.name: app config version bump for apk pin updates

packageRules.description: Automerge pkgrel-only apk pin bumps (the apk datasource's versioning classifies 1.22-r7 -> 1.22-r8 as patch): an Alpine rebuild of the same upstream release – the CLI is unchanged by definition, so no human review is needed (pkgver bumps are minor/major and stay manual via the next rule). Grouped into one branch (groupName): split packages built from one APKBUILD share pkgver and pkgrel and drift together, so per-package PRs would leave the sibling pin stale in each PR's own tree – the build's apk add cannot resolve it and the automerge deadlocks against the sibling PR; one grouped PR per upstream event carries every drifted pin and stays self-consistent. The changelog entry is added post-merge by the apk-bump workflow. Weekly batch cadence (same schedule strip as the tool/action rules) – pkgrel rebuilds lag at most one batch. Merged by GitHub's native auto-merge once branch protection's required checks are green (platformAutomerge; see repository-root KNOWLEDGE.md §"CI: Branch protection and platform-native automerge") – merges do not wait for the hosted Renovate app's run cadence. automergeStrategy rebase: linear history, one conventional commit per bump (GitHub replays the branch's single commit onto the tip at merge time); conflicts block the merge until Renovate rebases (same rationale as the supervisor-pin rule).

apk pkgver bumps (upstream version changes) may change CLI semantics – cf. hd-idle-genargs – so they keep human review: label and leave automerge off (patch bumps automerge via the previous rule). Grouped like the patch rule: one reviewed release per pkgver event, all drifted pins in one self-consistent tree.

Our own actions that follow a branch (like home-assistant/actions@master) float on purpose. Pinning them would open a digest PR in every repository for each change to them. Our own actions on a version tag are pinned like any other.

mise [tools] pins (mise manager; registry-backed: github/aqua/npm/core backends): weekly, same cadence as the actions manager. Renovate updates the pinned version and runs `mise lock` in safe mode so mise.lock stays in sync; the CI check job (hk lint gate + validate) validates the bumped toolset before merge.

hk pkl-package manager (custom.regex): same weekly Monday cadence and label as the mise [tools] rule so BOTH hk deps of the pair update together (mise manager owns mise.toml + mise.lock, this one hk.pkl) – a schedule mismatch would open one-sided desync PRs on off-Monday runs. Listed for both match spellings because the mise manager's dep matches packageRules by its resolved packageName jdx/hk, not the depName hk that PR titles show (verified against Renovate 44.235.0, 2026-11-12, local reproduction), and which side wins for custom-manager deps is not pinned down.

Supervisor schema pin: weekly batch cadence (same schedule strip as the tool/action rules), so the whole dependency batch opens Sunday evening and is merged before Monday 8am. The Renovate PR body lists the upstream changelog for an audit trail. Merged by GitHub's native auto-merge once branch protection's required checks are green (platformAutomerge; see repository-root KNOWLEDGE.md §"CI: Branch protection and platform-native automerge"). automergeStrategy rebase: linear history, one conventional commit per bump (GitHub replays the branch's single commit onto the tip at merge time); conflicts block the merge until Renovate rebases – same as manual.

Automerge minor and patch mise [tools] bumps once CI is green: the PR's check job runs the lint gate plus validate:apps on the toolset it installs, so green certifies the eagerly-installed tools against the repo exactly as they will run after merge – a release that newly fires rules fails the bump PR's own gate instead of landing, and later PRs run the same gate, so nothing slips through post-merge. mise-action's bare install skips lazy-declared tools (copilot, go, the go:-backend agent, vendir) – their bumps ride on the install's lockfile gate (mise-action adds --locked when a lockfile is present, so a mise.toml/mise.lock desync fails the check) rather than on tool execution. Majors keep human review: they can redefine semantics the config was verified against (hk's hk.pkl contract, renovate config flags, runtime majors like node/python/go).

Automerge minor and patch hk bumps for the mise-custom pair: Renovate folds mise.toml, mise.lock and hk.pkl into one branch anyway, and the check job runs hk itself – a green PR certifies the bumped hk plus the desync invariant (mise install --locked). Majors keep human review – hk majors may redefine the hk.pkl step contract this repo's lint gate is built on.

Automerge minor and patch updates of the digest-pinned actions that need no human review beyond the release-age gate: GitHub's own actions (the {/,}** glob covers subpath actions like actions/cache/save too) and jdx/mise-action, the one non-GitHub digest-pinned action the PR-path workflows execute (lint, apk-bump, action-bump-review) – green CI runs these exact action versions, so the bump is exercised before merge. Both gate on a 3-day minimum release age (a dependency cooldown) instead of an AI supply-chain review: the minified dist bundles are unreviewable in the compare API's diff, so the AI verdict would systematically fail closed – blocking automerge without adding signal – while not bumping well-maintained popular actions is the higher risk, and the cooldown provides the discovery window that matters at this scale. The actions org is owned and staff-maintained by GitHub – a verified org (checked via the GitHub API, 2026-11-16); mise-action rides the same gate on popularity and unreviewability, not org trust. The review workflow excludes these slugs from AI review to match. Keep the package list in sync when PR-path workflows gain digest-pinned actions outside GitHub's actions org; home-assistant/** is absent on purpose – the branch-following helpers under it float (see the pinDigests rule) and never produce digest bumps; home-assistant/builder is digest-pinned but stays manual (see below). Digest pinning stays; majors keep human review (runtime switches such as node20 → node24 ride major bumps); digest-typed updates (a ref repointed without a release) stay manual for every action – precisely the supply-chain signal a human should review. Everything else stays manual too: tj-actions/changed-files (see its rule), and the build-path actions home-assistant/builder and nick-fields/retry – these do run in PR CI whenever a PR touches build files (the full build matrix, minus publishing), but they execute with id-token: write and packages: write on the publish path and every one of their bumps triggers the whole multi-arch build matrix; privilege blast radius plus cost warrant human review.

Never automerge tj-actions/changed-files: its March 2025 tag-repoint compromise (CVE-2025-30066) dumped runner secrets into public workflow logs, and green CI cannot certify a new action version's integrity – the malicious payload executed without failing the run. Digest pinning plus human review of every ref change is the mitigation, and a digest-typed update (a ref repointed with no release) is exactly the event a human should see. Redundant with the automerge rules above on purpose: it keeps the rationale explicit as the automerge set broadens.
